lines.translation: #tr.en: ‘[@i{I}] @i{have acquired a friend, the counsellor} [@i{that I kept}] @i{seeing} [@i{in dreams},]

manuscripts.atf: {d#}en-ki#-du₁₀ ma-li-ka-am a-na-ku ša a-ta-ma-ru-šu# i#-[na šu-na-tim]

lines.translation: #tr.en: Enkidu, the counsellor that I kept seeing [in dreams!]’

variants.reconstruction: %n enkīdu | ana šâšim || issaqqaram | ana hari[mtim]

lines.translation: #tr.en: Enkidu said to her, to the harlot:
#tr.en: ‘Come, O harlot, let me do for you a favour,

variants.reconstruction:
%n aššum | terdîm | yâti | ana libbi (|) uruk | ribītu (|) mā[tim]
#note: See @bib{RN117@224}: “Uruk is commonly described as @i{ribītum} in Old Babylonian Gilgameš, but this line uses a longer form of the epithet. In Gilgames the phrase @i{ribītu mātim} also occurs (without Uruk) in the Pennsylvania tablet (OB II 214), where it is the scene of Enkidu’s first encounter with Gilgames.” See also @bib{RN127@28}: “The piece has since been baked but it was already very legible, and no new readings have emerged as a result of its conservation. One minor improvement has been made to the copy of the obverse, where the tail of the vertical wedge of @i{ma} is now visible at the end of l. 5′, confirming the reading @akk{ri-bi-tu# ma#-[tim]}.”

manuscripts.atf: aš-šum te-er-di-im ia-ti a-na li-ib-bi UNUG{ki#} ri-bi#-tu# ma#-[tim]

lines.translation: #tr.en: because you led me here, into Uruk-the-City-of-the-[Land,]

variants.reconstruction: %n aššum | tukallimīni | damqam | tappâm | yâti | ibra(m)

manuscripts.atf: aš-šum tu#-ka-li-mi-ni dam-qa₂-am TAB.BA-a-am ia-ti# ib-ra

lines.translation: #tr.en: because you showed me a fine companion, (showed) me a friend.’

manuscripts.atf: [x x x x x] x-ri-tim ša UNUG{ki} ri-bi-tim
[x x x x x x x]-nu# x x ni-ši-ma i-te-r[u-ub]
at-ta nu-hi-dam ia-š[i-im ...] x x a-n[a x x] x x

lines.translation: #tr.en: as for you, inform for me […] to …
#tr.en: You were born and grew [up] in the wild,
#tr.en: a lion [attacked] you and you experienced all.
